picks.style: latin oracular pastoral, panpipes, lyre, low drone, clear male voice, slow, prophetic, widening
picks.why: The Fourth Eclogue: the last age of the Sibyl's song, the golden race returning, untilled earth pouring out gifts. The most famous passage in Latin pastoral.

picks.style: incantation song, hand drum, plucked lyre, drone, close female voice, hypnotic, insistent refrain
picks.why: Built on a repeating refrain — draw Daphnis home — with baneful herbs, a man turned wolf, ashes thrown over the shoulder. A spell already shaped as a song.

picks.style: pastoral lament, single shepherd's pipe, sparse strings, weathered male voice, unhurried, aching
picks.why: The exile's farewell to his fields and goats, ending on my songs are sung — the emotional centre of Eclogue 1.

picks.style: roman comic love-patter, tibia pipes, plucked lyre, tambourine, leering male voice, quick, gleeful
picks.why: A cascade of absurd endearments — my sparrow-chick, my dove, my leveret — sung at a rival locked behind bars.

picks.style: roman wedding procession, double aulos, torch-lit drums, shouted refrain, festive, striding
picks.why: Ends on the actual hymenaeal cry, piper and torch and all: Io Hymen hymenaee!

picks.style: comic soliloquy song, solo lyre, dry male voice, mid-tempo, rueful, deadpan
picks.why: The slave who reasons himself out of hanging because rope costs money — a complete self-contained joke.

picks.style: late antique epitaph chant, low male voices, bare drone, no percussion, very slow, grave
picks.why: A whole verse epitaph: swift savage death, and a woman held together by qualities men think discordant.

picks.style: latin ekphrastic hymn, plainchant with organum, soft bells, luminous, slow, echoing
picks.why: The church of light — sun straying over gilded panels, sapphire stone bending through leek-green glass.

picks.style: late roman banquet song, lyre, aulos, hand drum, warm mixed voices, mid-tempo, sensuous
picks.why: A catalogue of the feast in short lines — crocus, cassia, marigolds, balsam, lamps raised into the vault. Pure rhythm and concrete nouns.

picks.style: welsh folk air, harp, soft fiddle, gentle male voice, lilting, unhurried
picks.why: A finished song with a returning line: no sheep, no boat, no coin, yet the Maid of Llanwellyn smiles sweetly on me.

picks.style: scots folk song, fiddle and small pipes, bright female voice, brisk, teasing, dance-lilt
picks.why: The wooer-at-e'en refrain drives the whole thing, and the Scots is broad, funny and singable.

picks.style: english pastoral ballad, acoustic guitar, low strings, warm alto, slow, homely, wintry
picks.why: The cock on the roost and the ploughman waking from his dream of gold — Baillie's plain domestic realism at its best.

picks.style: georgian sacred ode, chamber organ, viols, grave baritone, slow, valedictory
picks.why: His deathbed verses to Young: take the muse's latest spark, ere we drop into the dark — then the gulf, and why stand shivering on the shore.

picks.style: 18th-century glee, harpsichord, male trio, jovial, rolling, tavern warmth
picks.why: Comus speaking over the goblet — a drinking-room inscription that reads as a toast already set to music.

picks.style: georgian retirement ode, flute and harpsichord, clear soprano, graceful, moderate, pastoral
picks.why: Keep avarice and ambition far off; give me the branching vine, the woodbine, the evening dew. A complete wish, cleanly turned.

picks.style: english baroque air, harpsichord, viola da gamba, light soprano, unhurried, bright
picks.why: The Lesbian lute laid down for morning air and the verdant lawn — the ode's opening stands entirely on its own.

picks.style: greek comic anapaests, aulos, hand drum, jeering male chorus, brisk, sardonic
picks.why: Hermippus' mocking verses to the king of the Satyrs, gnashing his teeth as if bitten by fiery Cleon.

picks.style: german romantic lied, dark piano, low baritone, slow, sardonic, ominous
picks.why: Mephistopheles' wager in five lines: despise reason, take the lying spirit, and I shall have thee fast and sure.
